items.title: Generalizable neural signatures of emotional-context memory reactivation during sleep
items.author: Penelope A. Lewis
items.content: Auditory cues reactivate memories with negative or neutral contexts during human non-REM sleep. EEG classifiers trained on theta power decode the emotional context of reactivation, generalizing to new participants without fine-tuning.

items.title: Ubiquitin‑like modifications manipulate cancer biology and confer therapeutic potential
items.author: Weiwei Liu
items.content: Ji et al. review current evidence on how six ubiquitin-like modifications—SUMOylation, NEDDylation, ISGylation, UFMylation, FAT10ylation, and ATG8ylation—contribute to cancer hallmark maintenance and therapy resistance. These modifications are associated with dysregulated protein stability, subcellular localization, enzymatic activity, and proteinprotein interactions in tumors, although challenges remain in deciphering their cancertype-specific dependencies. The authors further summarize recent drug discovery efforts targeting the enzymes governing these modifications, highlighting emerging opportunities for novel cancer therapeutics, although significant hurdles persist in achieving isoform selectivity and minimizing on-target toxicity.
